thread:
Sam: FYI noticed a pattern: keys minted by our 'integration-importer' show up in the quota UI as project=(none) and sometimes get routed to tenant-default. This is causing chargebacks to go wrong and hammering the shared dedicated pool.
Rhea: ugh. Any recent deploys that touched key creation?
Sam: no deploys, this looks like an edge-case in the importer flow where we don't persist the project_id on the key record if the incoming payload uses legacy `org_id` field.
Diego: so auth service still returns 200 and request principal looks fine, but the downstream routing layer only reads keys table.created_project which is empty -> fallback to tenant default.
Nina: we have two problems: (1) DB schema isn't enforcing project on keys, and (2) routing/billing assumes created_project is always set. Need to make system tolerant.
Tom: proposal: write origin metadata into key metadata at mint time (enum: console/api/integration). Persist created_project_id when provided. Make routing lookup consult key.metadata.project_id before falling back to principal.
Sam: agree. Additional ask: store metadata in the fast lookup cache (redis) as well so the hot path doesn't do extra joins during request routing.
Rhea: for safety, keep the old behavior as fallback. Don't change routing order until we've backfilled keys and warmed cache.
Diego: backfill plan: 1) run a batch that populates keys.created_project from historical usage logs (auth.request_events) where the key was used and a project was present, 2) for keys with no provenance, mark created_project="unknown" and tag origin=integration.
Nina: telemetry: emit new metric `routing.key_project_presence_total{status="present|missing",origin="api|console|integration"}` and a counter for `billing.attribution_mismatch_total` when billing project != routing project.
Tom: UI: add a column in keys list "Project origin" with pill: ProjectName (from key) or "none" plus a small callout if project differs from billing project. Allow filter by "missing project".
Sam: rollout steps I propose: feature-flagged code that writes metadata + cache write, enable backfill job, enable routing read-of-metadata behind flag, monitor for mismatch, then flip. Canary percentages: 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%.
Rhea: add an alert: if `billing.attribution_mismatch_total` > 0.5% of total at any roll stage for 10m -> page. Also add a Grafana panel with a heatmap of keys with missing projects.
Diego: ops commands to investigate:
```sh
# tail requests showing key lookups
kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n prod -f | grep key_id=\n# query keys missing project
psql prod_billing -c "select id,created_at from keys where created_project is null limit 50;"
# sample auth events for a key
psql prod_events -c "select * from auth_events where key_id='sa_abc' order by ts desc limit 20;"
```
Nina: migration concerns: ensure backfill runs with a lock to avoid racing with live writes. Use a timestamp cutoff; don't overwrite existing created_project.
Tom: about metrics cardinality: keep origin enum only; for project presence metric use bucketed top-n projects for cost reports, but for the `key_project_presence_total` only include {status,origin}.
Sam: I'll open the RFC and break into tickets: auth-service change, cache schema, backfill job, routing update, UI changes, dashboards + alerts. Aiming for first canary next week.
metrics-bot: new alert rule created: billing-attribution-mismatch-high (threshold: 0.5%) by Rhea at 2026-03-11T14:22:00Z
Rhea: thanks. If anyone finds a noisy importer job that spikes api-origin keys, flag it immediately so we can pause the import until backfill completes.
Sam: noted. I'll post the RFC link here once created.
